deviation_mechanism: The initial symmetric quarter-wave configuration (R2, layers 1-18 fixed at 158.0/268.0 nm) maximized fundamental Bragg reflection, yielding the 0.9227 peak. Introducing asymmetric thickness perturbations altered optical path lengths, disrupting phase-matching across the stack. Aggressive compression of layer 8 from 267.900 nm (R2) to 259.142 nm (R3), combined with expansion of layer 17 from 148.000 nm to 155.795 nm, increased effective refractive index contrast mismatch, causing destructive interference collapse (0.0196 in R3). Stabilizing these outer layers in R4 (layer 8 anchored at 258.998 nm, layer 17 at 155.173 nm) partially restored constructive interference, producing a +0.421 rebound to 0.4406. The deviation is physically attributable to thin-film phase accumulation penalties when departing from lambda/4 periodicity, offset by gradual optimization of higher-order cavity modes.
